checks.statement_fidelity: (1) developing_theorem: dev : UniversalCover M x0 -> X an IsGXMorphism for the pulled-back structure, IsLocalHomeomorph, hol : Deck proj ->* G, dev (gamma z) = hol gamma . dev z, for every gamma and z. pi_1 form: developing_theorem_fundamentalGroup through deckHom. (2) developing_unique: there is a UNIQUE g with dev' = g . dev and hol' = g hol g^-1, which is stronger than the dispatch's 'unique-enough'. (3) developing_descends: trivial hol gives D : M -> X, an IsGXMorphism, with dev = D o proj. (4) developing_theorem_of_simplyConnected: existence, plus uniqueness up to a unique g. Hypotheses: IsAnalyticAction (faithful + rigid; this is l.293's 'analytically') and ContinuousConstSMul are carried. T2, second countability and connectedness/local connectedness of X are dropped. Connectedness of M is dropped except in (3), where it is needed: proj must be surjective. Nothing is vacuous: developing_theorem instantiates on M = R with translations (checked), exists_developingMap_translation is an inhabitant, and (3)'s hypotheses are met by any simply connected M. No structure field carries a conclusion. IsGXMorphism into X is read through chartedSpaceSelf (isGXMorphism_iff_model: near every point a translate of the chart). This matches the paper's own def:developing_map (l.1726: a developing map is an (a.e.) (G,X)-morphism to X).

summary: Builds clean, 0 sorry, standard axioms only. All four dispatch items are proved under the requested names. Uniqueness holds with a unique g, and analyticity of developing maps needs no Hausdorff hypothesis (via uniqueness of covering lifts). The (G,X)-morphism reading of 'developing map' is the paper's own (def:developing_map, l.1726). No hypothesis is vacuous: the theorem instantiates on the translation line. The REPORT statuses are honest: l.293 closed, l.344 partial with a proved counterexample to the literal reading. Only minor issues: the bookkeeping of LocPathConnectedSpace in (4) and in the l.344 row, a counterexample stated on R rather than on M̃, a heavy import, and API convenience.
